title: Fill missing values with column mean
instruction:
Define a function `fill_nan_with_mean(data)` that takes a 2D NumPy array (which may contain `np.nan` values) and **returns a new array** where each NaN is replaced with the mean of its column (using `np.nanmean`).

Do **not** modify the original array — create and return a copy.
starter_code:
import numpy as np

def fill_nan_with_mean(data):
    # Compute column means using np.nanmean with axis=0
    # Fill NaN values with the column mean
    # Return a copy with NaN replaced (don't modify original)
    pass
test_suite:
import numpy as np

def test_fill_basic():
    data = np.array([[1., 2., np.nan],
                     [4., np.nan, 6.],
                     [7., 8., 9.]])
    result = exercise.fill_nan_with_mean(data)
    expected = np.array([[1., 2., 7.5],
                         [4., 5., 6.],
                         [7., 8., 9.]])
    assert np.allclose(result, expected), f"Expected:\n{expected}\nGot:\n{result}"

def test_no_nan_values():
    data = np.array([[1., 2., 3.],
                     [4., 5., 6.]])
    result = exercise.fill_nan_with_mean(data)
    assert np.allclose(result, data), f"Array with no NaN should remain unchanged: {result}"

def test_all_nan_in_column():
    data = np.array([[1., np.nan],
                     [4., np.nan]])
    result = exercise.fill_nan_with_mean(data)
    col1_mean = np.nanmean(data[:, 1])
    assert np.isnan(col1_mean), "Column with all NaN should still have NaN after fill"
    assert np.isnan(result[0, 1]) and np.isnan(result[1, 1]), "All-NaN column should remain NaN after fill"

def test_single_row():
    data = np.array([[np.nan, 5., np.nan]])
    result = exercise.fill_nan_with_mean(data)
    col0_mean = np.nanmean(data[:, 0])
    col2_mean = np.nanmean(data[:, 2])
    if np.isnan(col0_mean):
        assert np.isnan(result[0, 0]), f"Expected NaN, got {result[0, 0]}"
    else:
        assert result[0, 0] == col0_mean, f"Expected {col0_mean}, got {result[0, 0]}"
    if np.isnan(col2_mean):
        assert np.isnan(result[0, 2]), f"Expected NaN, got {result[0, 2]}"
    else:
        assert result[0, 2] == col2_mean, f"Expected {col2_mean}, got {result[0, 2]}"
    assert result[0, 1] == 5.0, f"Expected 5.0, got {result[0, 1]}"

def test_does_not_modify_original():
    original = np.array([[1., np.nan], [3., 4.]])
    data_copy = original.copy()
    result = exercise.fill_nan_with_mean(original)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(original, data_copy), "The original array should not be modified"
solution_code:
import numpy as np

def fill_nan_with_mean(data):
    result = data.copy()
    col_mean = np.nanmean(data, axis=0)
    for col in range(result.shape[1]):
        mask = np.isnan(result[:, col])
        result[mask, col] = col_mean[col]
    return result

test_suite:
import numpy as np

def test_standardize_basic():
    data = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50], dtype=float)
    standardized, mean_val, std_val = exercise.standardize(data)
    expected = np.array([-1.41421356, -0.70710678, 0., 0.70710678, 1.41421356])
    assert np.allclose(standardized, expected, atol=1e-6), f"Expected {expected}, got {standardized}"
    assert abs(mean_val - 0.0) < 0.01, f"Expected mean ~0.0, got {mean_val}"
    assert abs(std_val - 1.0) < 0.01, f"Expected std ~1.0, got {std_val}"

def test_standardize_already_centered():
    data = np.array([-2., -1., 0., 1., 2.])
    standardized, mean_val, std_val = exercise.standardize(data)
    assert abs(mean_val - 0.0) < 0.01, f"Expected mean ~0.0, got {mean_val}"
    assert abs(std_val - 1.0) < 0.01, f"Expected std ~1.0, got {std_val}"

def test_standardize_single_value():
    data = np.array([42.], dtype=float)
    standardized, mean_val, std_val = exercise.standardize(data)
    assert np.isnan(standardized[0]) or standardized[0] == 0.0, \
        f"Single-element array std is 0, expected 0 or NaN, got {standardized[0]}"

def test_standardize_negative_values():
    data = np.array([-10., -5., 0., 5., 10.])
    standardized, mean_val, std_val = exercise.standardize(data)
    assert abs(mean_val - 0.0) < 0.01, f"Expected mean ~0.0, got {mean_val}"
    assert abs(std_val - 1.0) < 0.01, f"Expected std ~1.0, got {std_val}"
